question: Since 2011, in Spain, parents of children with serious illnesses have had the right to request a reduction in their working time of at least 50 %, while remaining on the same salary, in order to be able to take care of their children. However, that right is not being applied equally to all workers.
A group of public employees, thought to comprise some 500 families, has come together to report that they are facing considerable barriers in accessing paid leave to take care of their sick children.

Unlike their counterparts in the private sector, whose leave entitlements are managed by Social Security, public employees have to deal with additional red tape and encounter limitations as regards the duration of leave of that kind. This disparity amounts to severe discrimination because, owing to the lack of uniformity in the regulation of leave, it makes it difficult for them to exercise their rights1.
In the light of this state of affairs: What steps is the Commission taking to ensure compliance with Directive 2000/78/EC2 on equal treatment in employment?
